cases.title: fix(packet): release the header stream after read errors
cases.body:
## Summary

Wrap the header read in a context manager in `packet/header.py`. Add `tests/test_header.py` with a stream whose read raises, asserting context exit and error propagation.

## Why

A failed read currently skips the explicit close and can keep a file descriptor open. The context manager releases it on both return and exception paths.

## Validation plan

Run the new exception-path test, then read an ordinary eight-byte header and a shorter file to check that returned bytes are unchanged. These are proposed checks, not recorded execution.

## Scope

Short reads remain allowed and `OSError` still reaches the caller. This does not add retries or a header-length rule.

edits.before:
def read_header(path: str) -> bytes:
    stream = open(path, "rb")
    header = stream.read(8)
    stream.close()
    return header
edits.message: Close the header stream when reading raises

edits.after:
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import pytest

from packet.header import read_header


def test_read_error_exits_stream_context() -> None:
    stream = MagicMock()
    stream.__enter__.return_value = stream
    stream.read.side_effect = OSError("unreadable header")
    with patch("packet.header.open", return_value=stream):
        with pytest.raises(OSError, match="unreadable header"):
            read_header("sample.bin")
    stream.__exit__.assert_called_once()
edits.message: Add a regression case for header read failures

cases.review: `packet/header.py` now exits the file context even if `read(8)` raises and still returns short byte sequences unchanged. `tests/test_header.py` supplies a failing stream and checks both propagation and context exit; a normal-read fixture would complement that regression case.

cases.title: build(archive): stabilize release archive metadata
cases.body:
## Summary

Change `scripts/archive.sh` to sort tar entries, stamp them with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (zero if unset), and use numeric owner/group zero. Pipe through `gzip -n` to omit source-name and timestamp header metadata. Update `docs/releasing.md` with those rules and the GNU tar requirement.

## Reason

The same built files can currently acquire different archive hashes because packaging host metadata leaks into the output. Fixing this metadata allows a useful same-content reproducibility check.

## Validation plan

Package identical content after changing mtimes and creation order, compare SHA-256 hashes, then unpack both outputs and compare names and bytes. Repeat with an explicit SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and with it unset.

## Boundaries

The script requires GNU tar; this does not promise portable flags for other tar implementations. Contents and permission bits are unchanged, so differences in those inputs may still change the hash.

edits.message: Normalize tar metadata and omit gzip timestamps in release archives

edits.before:
# Release archive

Run `scripts/archive.sh package.tar.gz` from the repository root after building dist/.
The packaging host must provide tar and gzip.
edits.after:
# Release archive

Run `scripts/archive.sh package.tar.gz` from the repository root after building dist/.
The packaging host must provide GNU tar and gzip.
Archive entries are sorted by name, owned by numeric user/group 0, and timestamped from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (default 0).
Gzip headers omit the source name and timestamp. File contents and permission bits are not normalized.
edits.message: Document archive metadata rules and GNU tar dependency

cases.review: `scripts/archive.sh` normalizes entry order, mtime, and ownership, while gzip -n removes its header timestamp and source name. `docs/releasing.md` accurately records these settings, the zero epoch default, GNU tar, and the limits around content and modes. Before releasing, confirm the packaging image actually supplies GNU tar; the current patch alone does not settle that deployment question.

cases.title: refactor(cratebox)!: remove the compatibility require path
cases.body:
## Summary

Delete `lib/cratebox/compat.rb`, raise the gem version from 1.9.0 to 2.0.0 in `lib/cratebox/version.rb`, and revise `docs/loading.md` to show the supported loader and migration.

## Why

Maintaining two documented paths for the same client adds a duplicate entrypoint without a separate capability. Version 2 retires the alias and leaves one canonical loader.

## Breaking changes

`require "cratebox/compat"` will stop loading. Replace it with `require "cratebox/client"` before upgrading to 2.0.0. The client class and methods do not move; downstream applications must update their own require strings.

## Validation plan

Build and install the gem in a clean Ruby process, confirm the canonical require succeeds and exposes the same client, then verify the removed alias raises LoadError. Check that the packaged version reports 2.0.0 and that the migration example uses only the canonical path.

cases.title: feat(events): support optional trace identifiers in task payloads
cases.body:
## Summary

Allow optional `trace_id` in `schemas/task-event.schema.json`, constrained to 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Add `trace_id?: string` to the exported TypeScript TaskEvent interface. Add serialized examples with and without the field in `tests/task-event.examples.json`.

## Reason

Operations needs to correlate task events with trace records without requiring older producers to add a field immediately. Keeping task_id as the only required key preserves their existing payloads.

## Validation plan

Validate both supplied JSON examples, reject a short or uppercase trace ID and an unknown extra key, and compile TypeScript objects with and without trace_id. The patch supplies examples, not a runner or an executed-test claim.

## Limits and compatibility

No producer starts populating the field here. The schema checks the textual shape, not trace existence; the TypeScript string type alone does not enforce that shape. Existing valid payloads stay valid under the updated schema. Consumers using the older closed schema must update it before receiving payloads that contain the new field.

Existing payloads remain accepted; old closed-schema consumers need a schema update before new-field traffic.

cases.title: feat(events): support optional trace identifiers in task payloads
cases.body:
## Context

Operations cannot correlate task-event payloads with the collector's trace records. Older producers also cannot be upgraded all at once. This PR addresses that gap.

Sender retry behavior and transport encryption are outside this work.

## Validation pending

A validation plan will be supplied after the schema owner responds.
